title: Revisiting the shutdown problem
abstract: arXiv:2606.08296v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A key premise in leading arguments for existential risk from artificial intelligence is that malfunctioning artificial agents could not be easily shut down. This motivates the catastrophic shutdown problem of ensuring that agents can be shut down before causing an existential catastrophe. A range of arguments and theorems are offered to suggest that solving the catastrophic shutdown problem is difficult, bolstering arguments for existential risk and motivating a search for solutions to the catastrophic shutdown problem. This paper argues for two conclusions. First, existing arguments require substantial additional assumptions and evidence to play the desired role in motivating existential risk concerns. Second, concern for the catastrophic shutdown problem has led to technical solutions that impose a high safety tax on model performance. translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.08296v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：在关于人工智能存在性风险的主要论点中，一个关键前提是，功能异常的人工智能代理可能无法被轻易关闭。这引发了灾难性关闭问题，即确保在引发存在性灾难之前能够关闭这些代理。一系列论证和定理被提出，以表明解决灾难性关闭问题是困难的，从而加强了存在性风险的论点，并推动了对灾难性关闭问题解决方案的探索。本文论证了两个结论。首先，现有论证需要大量额外假设和证据，才能在其预期角色中支持存在性风险的担忧。其次，对灾难性关闭问题的关注导致了技术解决方案，这些方案对模型性能施加了高安全税。这些结果将研究重新导向已识别的假设，并为技术发展提供指导。
tldr: 本文重新审视了AI关闭问题，指出现有论证缺乏充分假设和证据，且相关技术方案以高性能代价为安全税，建议研究应聚焦于这些关键假设。
en_tdlr: This paper revisits the AI shutdown problem, arguing that existing arguments lack sufficient assumptions and evidence, while technical solutions impose a high safety tax on performance, redirecting research toward key assumptions.
